about.heading: About
about.summary: I'm a Computer Science student at the University at Buffalo, minoring in Robotics and Math. I work on field robotics at DRONESLab and lead autonomy work on student rover teams. I care most about robot software that holds up outside the lab: navigation, SLAM, teleoperation and safety-critical control.

Undergraduate researcher at DRONESLab, building open-source control software for Boston Dynamics Spot
Led autonomy for NASA LunaBotics and 15 engineers across 4 subteams at UB SpaceBulls

projects.name: Open-Spot: Spot Operator
projects.description: The control-stack part of open-spot, DRONESLab's open-source alternative to ROS 2/Nav2 for Boston Dynamics Spot. It has two parts: a Godot 4 operator GUI that runs on a Steam Deck, and a Python control daemon on a Jetson Orin AGX. They talk over a custom UDP protocol with CRC-16 checks, and safety-critical commands are resent until acknowledged. Also includes a failsafe watchdog, e-stop paths isolated from the rest of the system, and plugins that run in separate processes so a crash can't take the robot down.

projects.name: VISION-Inspect
projects.description: An extension of DRONESLab's VISION infrastructure-inspection system for Spot. Instead of sampling at fixed waypoints, the robot decides when to capture based on LiDAR and a vision-language model (VLM), which makes inspection coverage more efficient. Includes a zero-shot transfer experiment: a 12B VLM is fine-tuned on general defect data while all culvert data is held out for testing.

projects.name: Catan Agent
projects.description: A reinforcement learning agent for Settlers of Catan. A graph neural network encodes the board so the policy works across different board layouts. Training uses PPO, and opponent strength adjusts to the agent's win rate, which sped up convergence.
